title: Quinn Pauli:
headline: CureGRIN's scientist says the hard part out loud, most clinical trials fail, and then explains what a family group does about it: more shots on goal, and trials built around what matters to families.
story: Quinn Pauli is CureGRIN's Scientific Director. Nick filmed her on 8 Oct at Neurvati after the GRIN Therapeutics meeting. Her story is the honest one for donors and partners: most clinical trials fail, so CureGRIN works to maximize shots on goal. Then what a patient group brings that a drug company cannot buy: the family perspective, what matters most to families, and the in-person outreach to industry that can't be beat.

For donors and partners. It is not about trial dates, which drug, or how a medicine works. No drug name in the cut. Hopeful, never somber: the failure line is the hook, and every line after it is what CureGRIN does about it.

Loops: L1 “Then why keep trying?” opens 0:00 and closes at 0:04 (maximizing shots on goal). L2 “What does a parent group give a drug company?” opens 0:00 and closes in the button (in-person outreach, what families experience day to day). Stakes: whether a child can communicate, or walk with assistance. A trial designed around the wrong thing does not progress.
